sections.body: Fiji Rugby has partnered with Coca-Cola Europacific Partners to launch limited-edition collectable cans and bottles celebrating the Fiji Airways Men’s 7s team. The initiative aims to connect the country's passion for the sport with community inspiration.

sections.heading: England hooker Jamie Blamire returns from injury to start for Leicester
sections.body: England hooker Jamie Blamire has been handed a starting spot for Leicester Tigers in Friday's Slater Cup clash against Gloucester, marking his return from injury. The front-rower's recovery provides a timely boost for Steve Borthwick's national squad planning ahead of the upcoming autumn internationals. Blamire is joined in the Leicester line-up by fellow England internationals Freddie Steward and Jack van Poortvliet at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, with coach Geoff Parling welcoming the hooker's immediate impact.

lead.why: Jamie Blamire's return from injury to start for Leicester Tigers provides a key development for England's front-row options ahead of the autumn internationals.

sections.heading: England hooker Jamie Blamire starts for Leicester Tigers in Slater Cup return
sections.body: England hooker Jamie Blamire will return to the Leicester Tigers starting line-up for Friday’s Slater Cup clash with Gloucester at Welford Road. Blamire is one of five changes made by coach Geoff Parling after recovering from injury to join fellow internationals Joe Heyes and Freddie Steward in the XV. Captain Jack van Poortvliet also starts, though Adam Radwan is rotated to the replacements. For the visitors, England centre Will Joseph retains his midfield spot in a Gloucester side currently sitting top of the table.

lead.why: England hooker Jamie Blamire returns to the starting line-up for Leicester Tigers following an injury lay-off.

sections.heading: Henry Slade opens up on how Type 1 diabetes affects his career
sections.body: England centre Henry Slade has spoken openly about living with Type 1 diabetes, and he is clear it never stopped him believing he could play rugby. Slade was diagnosed as an 18-year-old, but he already knew the condition could be managed: his father John was diagnosed when Henry was six months old and had spent 18 years living with it by the time his son was diagnosed. "I didn't for one second think I can't play rugby," Slade said. The Mirror's interview suggests the condition has not held him back at the highest level.

lead.why: A new, England-relevant feature on an international centre, not already covered today; the Smith and Baxter item was run earlier and the Leicester piece is club-level.

sections.heading: Victor Wembanyama credits Provence Rugby for inspiring team spirit and camaraderie
sections.body: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama has highlighted his off-season training with Provence as a transformative experience for his own approach to team dynamics. The 22-year-old, who spent time with the French second-tier side to focus on physical and mental conditioning, praised the unity he witnessed within the rugby environment. "It was very inspiring to see the relationship between team-mates, coaches and fans," Wembanyama said of his time training with the club, where he participated in line-out drills and passing sessions.

sections.body: Bordeaux-Begles have been positioned as a standard-setter for elite club rugby following a critical assessment of the sport's global landscape by England internationals Dan Cole and Ben Youngs. While discussing the current hierarchy of professional teams, the pair excluded Super Rugby sides from their top 10 rankings. This perspective underlines the growing domestic influence of the Top 14, where Bordeaux-Begles currently hold the distinction of being the reigning double-winning champions of the Investec Champions Cup.

His test is not trophies alone but sides who still capture the imagination decades later, shaped as much by timing and circumstance as by results. For French fans, it is a reminder that the 1977 side still stirs the imagination decades on.

sections.heading: Ireland women secure dominant victory over Japan Sakura XV in Cork
sections.body: The Ireland women’s side completed a clean sweep of their two-match series against Japan, recording a convincing 43-19 win at Virgin Media Park last weekend. Having established dominance at the scrum and in phase play, Ireland successfully countered Japan’s defensive efforts. Flyhalf Dannah O’Brien proved pivotal, as her tactical kicking repeatedly pressured the Japanese backfield. This latest result sees the team maintain momentum in the WXV Global Series as they look to build upon their recent performances.

lead.why: It is the only fresh, positive result involving an Irish side in the current pack coverage.

sections.heading: Owen Doyle condemns Michael Hooper and Sir Steve Hansen regarding Piardi
sections.body: Former IRFU director of referees Owen Doyle has labelled recent comments from Michael Hooper and Sir Steve Hansen as “totally out of order.” The pair had suggested that World Rugby should prevent Italian official Andrea Piardi from refereeing future Australia matches, citing concerns over player and referee welfare. Doyle challenged this stance, arguing that the criticism levelled at Piardi following the Wallabies' win over the Springboks was misdirected, particularly as the referee contended with significant technical failures regarding TMO communications.

lead.why: It addresses a significant controversy in the international game involving an influential former Irish figure.

sections.heading: Ireland women beat Japan 43-19 in Cork for second weekend running
sections.body: Ireland women's side beat Japan 43-19 at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday 3 October, their second straight win over the Sakura XV after a 31-24 result in Galway. Rugby Asia 247 says fly-half Dannah O'Brien's kicking caused Japan's defence serious problems, and that Aoife Dalton had a superb half. The defeat leaves Japan winless in four straight matches, and they head back home to face Wales twice in the WXV Global Series.

lead.why: The only fresh item in the pack, and it is an Ireland story: the women's side beating Japan again in WXV Global, though it is women's rugby and labelled as such.

sections.heading: Brain injury legal action faces ongoing threat of collapse this month
sections.body: The high-profile legal action regarding brain injuries in rugby remains in a precarious position as claimants continue to face a significant £2.8m legal bill. While recent court battles have prevented the cases from being thrown out, the financial burden remains the primary obstacle to the proceedings continuing. With the deadline to settle these mounting legal fees approaching this month, the future of the litigation against governing bodies remains uncertain for all parties involved, including those within the Scottish game.

sections.body: Claimants in rugby's brain injury litigation face a £2.8m legal bill to keep the case going, according to a Guardian report, and the action stays open until that cost is settled by the claimants this month. Earlier coverage, reported in August, had World Rugby and UK governing bodies losing their attempt to have the cases thrown out of court. A separate headline warns the action faces a threat of collapse, but the pack gives no detail or date for it. The pack does not say whether any Scotland-qualified players are among the claimants, so Scotland's link to the case is unconfirmed.

sections.body: The Ospreys will hand a debut to Wallabies star Marika Koroibete on the wing for their URC visit to Rodney Parade. Dragons boss Filo Tiatia has responded to his side's recent win over the Scarlets by making three changes to his starting XV, including the inclusion of Tongan international Fetuli Paea at outside centre. Harry Beddall also earns a start in the pack for a Dragons side looking to build momentum, while the Ospreys search for their first victory of the season.

sections.heading: Wales back Max Llewellyn returns to Gloucester bench for Slater Cup
sections.body: Welsh international Max Llewellyn has been named among the replacements for Gloucester ahead of Friday night's Slater Cup clash against Leicester Tigers. The midfielder’s return to the matchday squad provides a boost for the visitors as they look to maintain their unbeaten start to the season. Gloucester currently sit at the top of the log and seek a third consecutive victory at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, facing a Leicester side bolstered by the return of several high-profile internationals.

sections.heading: Dave Reddin recommits to WRU plan to scrap a region by 2028
sections.body: Dave Reddin has recommitted to the WRU plan to scrap one of Wales' four regional teams by 2028, a stance the Guardian reported at the end of September. Cardiff and the Dragons have been told they are safe, leaving the Scarlets and Ospreys to fight for the one remaining slot. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies calls the process "chaos", noting the union has moved from four teams to two and then to three. For Wales, the stakes include two western sides that between them have turned out hundreds of Test players.

lead.why: Of the shortlist, it is the most consequential story for Welsh rugby's structure, and the two fresher items are club-level or already reported.

sections.heading: Argentina formally submits technical proposal to host 2035 Rugby World Cup
sections.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has officially submitted all technical documentation required for its joint 2035 Rugby World Cup bid alongside Uruguay, Chile, and Brazil. The proposed plan outlines a multi-nation hosting model utilising eight Argentine stadiums, alongside marquee venues like the Maracanã in Brazil and Montevideo’s Centenario. World Rugby is currently conducting site feasibility studies, with a preferred host due to be identified in May 2027 before the final Council decision later that year. The region faces competition from Japan and Spain.

lead.why: The UAR has officially submitted the required technical documentation for the 2035 World Cup bid.

sections.heading: Argentina overpower Wales with dominant five-try display in Nations Championship
sections.body: Argentina showcased their attacking potential in the Nations Championship by securing a 35-21 victory over Wales. Despite a defeat to Scotland in the tournament opener, the Pumas recovered to brush aside the Welsh challenge in San Juan. The result highlighted a clinical side that scored five tries, effectively halting a mini-revival from the visitors. The win offers a boost to the squad as they continue their campaign, having also navigated a testing loss to England during the competition.

lead.why: The report provides fresh context regarding Argentina's recent Nations Championship performance against Wales.

sections.heading: Argentina run in five tries to beat Wales 35-21 in San Juan
sections.body: Argentina's 35-21 win over Wales in San Juan was the Pumas brushing aside their opening-weekend defeat to Scotland, with a dominant five-try display against three Welsh tries. It is the only win on Argentina's Nations Championship record so far, and it sits well apart from the 24-31 loss to England. Today's coverage offers no fresh team news ahead of the Ireland match.

sections.heading: Les Kiss keeps Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on wing for Eden Park Test
sections.body: Les Kiss has kept faith with the side that beat South Africa 42-38 in Perth, changing only one starter for Saturday's first Bledisloe Cup Test. Inside centre Hunter Paisami is out serving a four-week ban for a high tackle, so Isaac Henry, a four-Test Queensland Reds midfielder, starts at 13 with Len Ikitau moving to 12 after passing a fitness test on an ankle. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii stays on the wing, where he shone under the high ball in Perth. "We just wanted to persist with that continuity of that back three," Kiss said.

sections.heading: Japan Sakura XV leave Europe winless following second Irish defeat
sections.body: The Sakura XV concluded their European tour without a victory after falling 19-43 to Ireland at Virgin Media Park. Despite a strong opening—leading 7-0 after a Sakurako Korai try—the team struggled against Irish set-piece dominance and a clinical kicking game. Japan now returns home to prepare for a two-match series against Wales. Head coach Toshizumi Kitagawa previously noted the importance of trusting their attacking identity against higher-ranked opponents, a mantra they will need to refine ahead of these upcoming encounters.

lead.why: The Sakura XV's winless tour of Europe is the most significant recent result for Japan's international programme.

sections.heading: Japan Sakura 7s Reclaim Gold at the 20th Asian Games Tournament
sections.body: Japan’s women secured a notable victory at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, defeating defending champions China 10-5 in a tightly contested final. The result marks the first time the Sakura 7s have reclaimed the gold medal since their success two Games ago. While the Japanese men’s side settled for bronze after a 17-5 win over Korea, the women’s triumph highlighted a competitive weekend of sevens, with the hosts overcoming a resilient Chinese team to secure the top podium spot.

lead.why: This is a new development regarding the Sakura 7s reclaiming gold at the Asian Games.

sections.heading: Japan women's sevens beat China 10-5 to reclaim Asian Games gold
sections.body: Japan's women's sevens side reclaimed the Asian Games gold they last won two Games ago, beating defending champions China 10-5 in another close final between the two. Rugby Asia 247 reports that the Japan men took bronze after losing their semi-final 10-7 to China, then beating Korea 17-5 in the third-place play-off. Hong Kong China completed a men's treble, but the story for Japan is a women's title won with a tight defence and a one-score margin.

lead.why: It is a new development for Japan that has not appeared on this tab, and it is a result a fan would want to talk about.

sections.heading: Damian McKenzie starts at flyhalf as Richie Mo'unga misses Bledisloe tests
sections.body: Damian McKenzie will shift from fullback to flyhalf for Saturday’s opening Bledisloe Cup clash at Eden Park after Richie Mo'unga was ruled out of the entire series. Mo'unga sustained a calf tear during training on Tuesday, forcing a late reshuffle of the backline. Beauden Barrett will slot in at fullback for his first start of the year. Dave Rennie described the injury as "disappointing for the group" but noted that his playmakers remain highly interchangeable in the team’s current structure.

sections.heading: Richie Mo'unga ruled out of both Bledisloe Tests with calf tear
sections.body: Richie Mo'unga will miss both Bledisloe Cup Tests with a calf tear sustained in training on Tuesday, after he had initially been named in the starting XV. Rennie said: "We named Richie to the squad on Monday, and he got injured on Tuesday, which is disappointing for him and disappointing for the group." Damian McKenzie moves to flyhalf, with Beauden Barrett at No. 15 for the opening Test, and no injury replacement has been decided for Mo'unga.

sections.heading: Steve Lancaster says South African Super Rugby return is not being discussed
sections.body: NZ Rugby chief executive Steve Lancaster says South African teams returning to Super Rugby is not on the agenda for now. He has not ruled the idea out, but told DSPN there are no discussions under way, and that South Africa are committed to the United Rugby Championship for a period of time he could not pin down. Lancaster described the two unions as "really tight" after the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series, which the Springboks took 3-1.

lead.why: It is a fresh, South Africa-facing men's union-level quote from NZ Rugby's chief, and the other live items are either already read or club or NZ-focused.
